audit_status.source_base: Greek Acts text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Saul encounter, Ananias, Damascus witness, escape, Jerusalem acceptance, Aeneas healing, Tabitha raising.

verses.restored: Saul, still breathing threat and murder against the disciples of the Lord, went to the high priest,

familiar.text: And Saul, yet breathing out threatenings and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, went unto the high priest,

modern.text: Meanwhile, Saul was still breathing out murderous threats against the disciples of the Lord. He approached the high priest

original.text: Ὁ δὲ Σαῦλος ἔτι ἐμπνέων ἀπειλῆς καὶ φόνου εἰς τοὺς μαθητὰς τοῦ κυρίου, προσελθὼν τῷ ἀρχιερεῖ

verses.restored: and asked from him letters to Damascus for the synagogues, so that if he found any belonging to the Way, both men and women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem.

familiar.text: And desired of him letters to Damascus to the synagogues, that if he found any of this way, whether they were men or women, he might bring them bound unto Jerusalem.

modern.text: and requested letters to the synagogues in Damascus, so that if he found any men or women belonging to the Way, he could bring them as prisoners to Jerusalem.

original.text: ᾐτήσατο παρʼ αὐτοῦ ἐπιστολὰς εἰς Δαμασκὸν πρὸς τὰς συναγωγάς, ὅπως ἐάν τινας εὕρῃ τῆς ὁδοῦ ὄντας, ἄνδρας τε καὶ γυναῖκας, δεδεμένους ἀγάγῃ εἰς Ἰερουσαλήμ.

verses.restored: As he journeyed, it happened that he drew near to Damascus, and suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him.

familiar.text: And as he journeyed, he came near Damascus: and suddenly there shined round about him a light from heaven:

modern.text: As Saul drew near to Damascus on his journey, suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him.

original.text: ἐν δὲ τῷ πορεύεσθαι ἐγένετο αὐτὸν ἐγγίζειν τῇ Δαμασκῷ, ⸂ἐξαίφνης τε αὐτὸν περιήστραψεν⸃ φῶς ⸀ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ,

verses.restored: Falling upon the ground, he heard a voice saying to him, Saul, Saul, why do you pursue me?

familiar.text: And he fell to the earth, and heard a voice saying unto him, Saul, Saul, why persecutest thou me?

modern.text: He fell to the ground and heard a voice say to him, “Saul, Saul, why do you persecute Me?”

original.text: καὶ πεσὼν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἤκουσεν φωνὴν λέγουσαν αὐτῷ Σαοὺλ Σαούλ, τί με διώκεις;

verses.restored: He said, Who are you, Lord? He said, I am Jesus, whom you pursue.

familiar.text: And he said, Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said, I am Jesus whom thou persecutest: it is hard for thee to kick against the pricks.

modern.text: “Who are You, Lord?” Saul asked. “I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting,” He replied.

original.text: εἶπεν δέ· Τίς εἶ, κύριε; ὁ ⸀δέ· Ἐγώ εἰμι Ἰησοῦς ὃν σὺ διώκεις·

verses.restored: But rise and enter the city, and it will be spoken to you what you must do.

familiar.text: And he trembling and astonished said, Lord, what wilt thou have me to do? And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the city, and it shall be told thee what thou must do.

modern.text: “Now get up and go into the city, and you will be told what you must do.”

original.text: ἀλλὰ ἀνάστηθι καὶ εἴσελθε εἰς τὴν πόλιν, καὶ λαληθήσεταί σοι ⸂ὅ τί⸃ σε δεῖ ποιεῖν.

verses.restored: The men traveling with him stood speechless, hearing the voice but beholding no one.

familiar.text: And the men which journeyed with him stood speechless, hearing a voice, but seeing no man.

modern.text: The men traveling with Saul stood there speechless. They heard the voice but did not see anyone.

original.text: οἱ δὲ ἄνδρες οἱ συνοδεύοντες αὐτῷ εἱστήκεισαν ἐνεοί, ἀκούοντες μὲν τῆς φωνῆς μηδένα δὲ θεωροῦντες.

verses.restored: Saul rose from the ground, and though his eyes were opened, he saw nothing. Leading him by the hand, they brought him into Damascus.

familiar.text: And Saul arose from the earth; and when his eyes were opened, he saw no man: but they led him by the hand, and brought him into Damascus.

modern.text: Saul got up from the ground, but when he opened his eyes he could not see a thing. So they led him by the hand into Damascus.

original.text: ἠγέρθη δὲ ⸀Σαῦλος ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς, ἀνεῳγμένων ⸀δὲ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν αὐτοῦ ⸀οὐδὲν ἔβλεπεν· χειραγωγοῦντες δὲ αὐτὸν εἰσήγαγον εἰς Δαμασκόν.

verses.restored: He was three days not seeing, and he neither ate nor drank.

familiar.text: And he was three days without sight, and neither did eat nor drink.

modern.text: For three days he was without sight, and he did not eat or drink anything. Ananias Baptizes Saul

original.text: καὶ ἦν ἡμέρας τρεῖς μὴ βλέπων, καὶ οὐκ ἔφαγεν οὐδὲ ἔπιεν.

verses.restored: There was a certain disciple in Damascus named Ananias. The Lord said to him in a vision, Ananias. He said, Look, I am here, Lord.

familiar.text: And there was a certain disciple at Damascus, named Ananias; and to him said the Lord in a vision, Ananias. And he said, Behold, I am here, Lord.

modern.text: In Damascus there was a disciple named Ananias. The Lord spoke to him in a vision, “Ananias!” “Here I am, Lord,” he answered.

original.text: Ἦν δέ τις μαθητὴς ἐν Δαμασκῷ ὀνόματι Ἁνανίας, καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτὸν ⸂ἐν ὁράματι ὁ κύριος⸃· Ἁνανία. ὁ δὲ εἶπεν· Ἰδοὺ ἐγώ, κύριε.

verses.restored: The Lord said to him, Rise and go to the street called Straight, and seek in the house of Judas a man from Tarsus named Saul; for look, he is praying.

familiar.text: And the Lord said unto him, Arise, and go into the street which is called Straight, and enquire in the house of Judas for one called Saul, of Tarsus: for, behold, he prayeth,

modern.text: “Get up!” the Lord told him. “Go to the house of Judas on Straight Street and ask for a man from Tarsus named Saul, for he is praying.

original.text: ὁ δὲ κύριος πρὸς αὐτόν· ⸀Ἀναστὰς πορεύθητι ἐπὶ τὴν ῥύμην τὴν καλουμένην Εὐθεῖαν καὶ ζήτησον ἐν οἰκίᾳ Ἰούδα Σαῦλον ὀνόματι Ταρσέα, ἰδοὺ γὰρ προσεύχεται,

verses.restored: He has seen a man named Ananias coming in and laying hands on him so that he might see again.

familiar.text: And hath seen in a vision a man named Ananias coming in, and putting his hand on him, that he might receive his sight.

modern.text: In a vision he has seen a man named Ananias come and place his hands on him to restore his sight.”

original.text: καὶ εἶδεν ⸂ἄνδρα ἐν ὁράματι Ἁνανίαν ὀνόματι⸃ εἰσελθόντα καὶ ἐπιθέντα αὐτῷ ⸀χεῖρας ὅπως ἀναβλέψῃ.

verses.restored: Ananias answered, Lord, I have heard from many about this man, how many harmful things he did to your holy ones in Jerusalem.

familiar.text: Then Ananias answered, Lord, I have heard by many of this man, how much evil he hath done to thy saints at Jerusalem:

modern.text: But Ananias answered, “Lord, many people have told me about this man and all the harm he has done to Your saints in Jerusalem.

original.text: ἀπεκρίθη δὲ Ἁνανίας· Κύριε, ⸀ἤκουσα ἀπὸ πολλῶν περὶ τοῦ ἀνδρὸς τούτου, ὅσα κακὰ ⸂τοῖς ἁγίοις σου ἐποίησεν⸃ ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ·

verses.restored: And here he has authority from the chief priests to bind all who call upon your name.

familiar.text: And here he hath authority from the chief priests to bind all that call on thy name.

modern.text: And now he is here with authority from the chief priests to arrest all who call on Your name.”

original.text: καὶ ὧδε ἔχει ἐξουσίαν παρὰ τῶν ἀρχιερέων δῆσαι πάντας τοὺς ἐπικαλουμένους τὸ ὄνομά σου.

verses.restored: But the Lord said to him, Go, because this one is a chosen vessel to me, to carry my name before nations and kings and children of Israel.

familiar.text: But the Lord said unto him, Go thy way: for he is a chosen vessel unto me, to bear my name before the Gentiles, and kings, and the children of Israel:

modern.text: “Go!” said the Lord. “This man is My chosen instrument to carry My name before the Gentiles and their kings, and before the people of Israel.

original.text: εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν ὁ κύριος· Πορεύου, ὅτι σκεῦος ἐκλογῆς ⸂ἐστίν μοι⸃ οὗτος τοῦ βαστάσαι τὸ ὄνομά μου ἐνώπιον ⸀ἐθνῶν ⸀τε καὶ βασιλέων υἱῶν τε Ἰσραήλ,

verses.restored: For I will show him how much it is necessary for him to suffer for my name.

familiar.text: For I will shew him how great things he must suffer for my name’s sake.

modern.text: I will show him how much he must suffer for My name.”

original.text: ἐγὼ γὰρ ὑποδείξω αὐτῷ ὅσα δεῖ αὐτὸν ὑπὲρ τοῦ ὀνόματός μου παθεῖν.

verses.restored: Ananias went away and entered the house; laying hands on him, he said, Brother Saul, the Lord Jesus, the one who appeared to you on the road by which you came, has sent me so that you may see again and be filled with holy Spirit.

familiar.text: And Ananias went his way, and entered into the house; and putting his hands on him said, Brother Saul, the Lord, even Jesus, that appeared unto thee in the way as thou camest, hath sent me, that thou mightest receive thy sight, and be filled with the Holy Ghost.

modern.text: So Ananias went to the house, and when he arrived, he placed his hands on Saul. “Brother Saul,” he said, “the Lord Jesus, who appeared to you on the road as you were coming here, has sent me so that you may see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”

original.text: ἀπῆλθεν δὲ Ἁνανίας καὶ εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὴν οἰκίαν, καὶ ἐπιθεὶς ἐπʼ αὐτὸν τὰς χεῖρας εἶπεν· Σαοὺλ ἀδελφέ, ὁ κύριος ἀπέσταλκέν με, ⸀Ἰησοῦς ὁ ὀφθείς σοι ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ ᾗ ἤρχου, ὅπως ἀναβλέψῃς καὶ πλησθῇς πνεύματος ἁγίου.

verses.restored: Immediately something like scales fell from his eyes, and he saw again. Rising, he was baptized,

familiar.text: And immediately there fell from his eyes as it had been scales: and he received sight forthwith, and arose, and was baptized.

modern.text: At that instant, something like scales fell from Saul’s eyes, and his sight was restored. He got up and was baptized,

original.text: καὶ εὐθέως ἀπέπεσαν ⸂αὐτοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν ὀφθαλμῶν⸃ ⸀ὡς λεπίδες, ἀνέβλεψέν τε καὶ ἀναστὰς ἐβαπτίσθη,

verses.restored: and taking food, he was strengthened. He was with the disciples in Damascus some days.

familiar.text: And when he had received meat, he was strengthened. Then was Saul certain days with the disciples which were at Damascus.

modern.text: and after taking some food, he regained his strength. And he spent several days with the disciples in Damascus. Saul Preaches at Damascus

original.text: καὶ λαβὼν τροφὴν ⸀ἐνίσχυσεν. Ἐγένετο ⸀δὲ μετὰ τῶν ἐν Δαμασκῷ μαθητῶν ἡμέρας τινὰς,

verses.restored: Immediately in the synagogues he proclaimed Jesus, that this one is the Son of the Divine.

familiar.text: And straightway he preached Christ in the synagogues, that he is the Son of God.

modern.text: Saul promptly began to proclaim Jesus in the synagogues, declaring, “He is the Son of God.”

original.text: καὶ εὐθέως ἐν ταῖς συναγωγαῖς ἐκήρυσσεν τὸν ⸀Ἰησοῦν ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: All who heard were amazed and said, Is this not the one who ravaged those calling on this name in Jerusalem, and came here for this purpose, to bring them bound to the chief priests?

familiar.text: But all that heard him were amazed, and said; Is not this he that destroyed them which called on this name in Jerusalem, and came hither for that intent, that he might bring them bound unto the chief priests?

modern.text: All who heard him were astounded and asked, “Isn’t this the man who wreaked havoc in Jerusalem on those who call on this name? And hasn’t he come here to take them as prisoners to the chief priests?”

original.text: ἐξίσταντο δὲ πάντες οἱ ἀκούοντες καὶ ἔλεγον· Οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ πορθήσας ⸀ἐν Ἰερουσαλὴμ τοὺς ἐπικαλουμένους τὸ ὄνομα τοῦτο, καὶ ὧδε εἰς τοῦτο ἐληλύθει ἵνα δεδεμένους αὐτοὺς ἀγάγῃ ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀρχιερεῖς;

verses.restored: But Saul was being empowered more and more and confounding the Judeans dwelling in Damascus, proving that this one is the Messiah.

familiar.text: But Saul increased the more in strength, and confounded the Jews which dwelt at Damascus, proving that this is very Christ.

modern.text: But Saul was empowered all the more, and he confounded the Jews living in Damascus by proving that Jesus is the Christ. The Escape from Damascus

original.text: Σαῦλος δὲ μᾶλλον ἐνεδυναμοῦτο καὶ ⸀συνέχυννεν ⸀τοὺς Ἰουδαίους τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐν Δαμασκῷ, συμβιβάζων ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ χριστός.

verses.restored: When many days were fulfilled, the Judeans took counsel to kill him.

familiar.text: And after that many days were fulfilled, the Jews took counsel to kill him:

modern.text: After many days had passed, the Jews conspired to kill him,

original.text: Ὡς δὲ ἐπληροῦντο ἡμέραι ἱκαναί, συνεβουλεύσαντο οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι ἀνελεῖν αὐτόν·

verses.restored: Their plot became known to Saul. They were also watching the gates day and night so that they might kill him.

familiar.text: But their laying await was known of Saul. And they watched the gates day and night to kill him.

modern.text: but Saul learned of their plot. Day and night they watched the city gates in order to kill him.

original.text: ἐγνώσθη δὲ τῷ Σαύλῳ ἡ ἐπιβουλὴ αὐτῶν. ⸂παρετηροῦντο δὲ καὶ⸃ τὰς πύλας ἡμέρας τε καὶ νυκτὸς ὅπως αὐτὸν ἀνέλωσιν·

verses.restored: But his disciples, taking him by night, let him down through the wall, lowering him in a basket.

familiar.text: Then the disciples took him by night, and let him down by the wall in a basket.

modern.text: One night, however, his disciples took him and lowered him in a basket through a window in the wall. Saul in Jerusalem

original.text: λαβόντες δὲ ⸂οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ⸃ νυκτὸς ⸂διὰ τοῦ τείχους καθῆκαν αὐτὸν⸃ χαλάσαντες ἐν σπυρίδι.

verses.restored: Arriving in Jerusalem, he was attempting to join the disciples, and all were afraid of him, not trusting that he was a disciple.

familiar.text: And when Saul was come to Jerusalem, he assayed to join himself to the disciples: but they were all afraid of him, and believed not that he was a disciple.

modern.text: When Saul arrived in Jerusalem, he tried to join the disciples, but they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.

original.text: Παραγενόμενος δὲ ⸀εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ ⸀ἐπείραζεν κολλᾶσθαι τοῖς μαθηταῖς· καὶ πάντες ἐφοβοῦντο αὐτόν, μὴ πιστεύοντες ὅτι ἐστὶν μαθητής.

verses.restored: But Barnabas took him, brought him to the apostles, and described to them how on the road he saw the Lord, that he spoke to him, and how in Damascus he spoke boldly in the name of Jesus.

familiar.text: But Barnabas took him, and brought him to the apostles, and declared unto them how he had seen the Lord in the way, and that he had spoken to him, and how he had preached boldly at Damascus in the name of Jesus.

modern.text: Then Barnabas brought him to the apostles and described how Saul had seen the Lord, who spoke to him on the road to Damascus, and how Saul had spoken boldly in that city in the name of Jesus.

original.text: Βαρναβᾶς δὲ ἐπιλαβόμενος αὐτὸν ἤγαγεν πρὸς τοὺς ἀποστόλους, καὶ διηγήσατο αὐτοῖς πῶς ἐν τῇ ὁδῷ εἶδεν τὸν κύριον καὶ ὅτι ἐλάλησεν αὐτῷ καὶ πῶς ἐν Δαμασκῷ ἐπαρρησιάσατο ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι ⸀τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.

verses.restored: He was with them, going in and out in Jerusalem, speaking boldly in the name of the Lord.

familiar.text: And he was with them coming in and going out at Jerusalem.

modern.text: So Saul stayed with them, moving about freely in Jerusalem and speaking boldly in the name of the Lord.

original.text: καὶ ἦν μετʼ αὐτῶν εἰσπορευόμενος ⸂καὶ ἐκπορευόμενος⸃ εἰς ⸀Ἰερουσαλήμ, παρρησιαζόμενος ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ ⸀κυρίου,

verses.restored: He was speaking and disputing with the Hellenists, but they were attempting to kill him.

familiar.text: And he spake boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus, and disputed against the Grecians: but they went about to slay him.

modern.text: He talked and debated with the Grecian Jews, but they tried to kill him.

original.text: ἐλάλει τε καὶ συνεζήτει πρὸς τοὺς Ἑλληνιστάς· οἱ δὲ ἐπεχείρουν ⸂ἀνελεῖν αὐτόν⸃.

verses.restored: The siblings, learning this, brought him down to Caesarea and sent him away to Tarsus.

familiar.text: Which when the brethren knew, they brought him down to Caesarea, and sent him forth to Tarsus.

modern.text: When the brothers learned of this, they took him down to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus. The Healing of Aeneas

original.text: ἐπιγνόντες δὲ οἱ ἀδελφοὶ κατήγαγον αὐτὸν εἰς Καισάρειαν καὶ ἐξαπέστειλαν αὐτὸν εἰς Ταρσόν.

verses.restored: Therefore the assembly throughout all Judea and Galilee and Samaria had peace, being built up; walking in the reverence of the Lord and in the comfort/encouragement of the holy Spirit, it multiplied.

familiar.text: Then had the churches rest throughout all Judaea and Galilee and Samaria, and were edified; and walking in the fear of the Lord, and in the comfort of the Holy Ghost, were multiplied.

modern.text: Then the church throughout Judea, Galilee, and Samaria experienced a time of peace. It grew in strength and numbers, living in the fear of the Lord and the encouragement of the Holy Spirit.

original.text: ⸂Ἡ μὲν οὖν ἐκκλησία καθʼ ὅλης τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ Γαλιλαίας καὶ Σαμαρείας εἶχεν εἰρήνην οἰκοδομουμένη, καὶ πορευομένη τῷ φόβῳ τοῦ κυρίου καὶ τῇ παρακλήσει τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ἐπληθύνετο⸃.

verses.restored: It happened that Peter, passing through all, came down also to the holy ones dwelling in Lydda.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, as Peter passed throughout all quarters, he came down also to the saints which dwelt at Lydda.

modern.text: As Peter traveled throughout the area, he went to visit the saints in Lydda.

original.text: Ἐγένετο δὲ Πέτρον διερχόμενον διὰ πάντων κατελθεῖν καὶ πρὸς τοὺς ἁγίους τοὺς κατοικοῦντας Λύδδα.

verses.restored: There he found a certain man named Aeneas, who had been lying on a mat eight years and was paralyzed.

familiar.text: And there he found a certain man named Aeneas, which had kept his bed eight years, and was sick of the palsy.

modern.text: There he found a man named Aeneas, who had been paralyzed and bedridden for eight years.

original.text: εὗρεν δὲ ἐκεῖ ἄνθρωπόν τινα ⸂ὀνόματι Αἰνέαν⸃ ἐξ ἐτῶν ὀκτὼ κατακείμενον ἐπὶ ⸀κραβάττου, ὃς ἦν παραλελυμένος.

verses.restored: Peter said to him, Aeneas, Jesus Messiah heals you; rise and make your bed. Immediately he rose.

familiar.text: And Peter said unto him, Aeneas, Jesus Christ maketh thee whole: arise, and make thy bed. And he arose immediately.

modern.text: “Aeneas,” Peter said to him, “Jesus Christ heals you! Get up and put away your mat.” Immediately Aeneas got up,

original.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ ὁ Πέτρος· Αἰνέα, ἰᾶταί σε Ἰησοῦς ⸀Χριστός· ἀνάστηθι καὶ στρῶσον σεαυτῷ· καὶ εὐθέως ἀνέστη.

verses.restored: All those dwelling in Lydda and Sharon saw him, and they turned to the Lord.

familiar.text: And all that dwelt at Lydda and Saron saw him, and turned to the Lord.

modern.text: and all who lived in Lydda and Sharon saw him and turned to the Lord. The Raising of Tabitha (John 11:38–44)

original.text: καὶ εἶδαν αὐτὸν πάντες οἱ κατοικοῦντες Λύδδα καὶ τὸν ⸀Σαρῶνα, οἵτινες ἐπέστρεψαν ἐπὶ τὸν κύριον.

verses.restored: In Joppa there was a certain disciple named Tabitha, which translated is called Dorcas. She was full of good works and acts of mercy that she was doing.

familiar.text: Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha, which by interpretation is called Dorcas: this woman was full of good works and almsdeeds which she did.

modern.text: In Joppa there was a disciple named Tabitha (which is translated as Dorcas), who was always occupied with works of kindness and charity.

original.text: Ἐν Ἰόππῃ δέ τις ἦν μαθήτρια ὀνόματι Ταβιθά, ἣ διερμηνευομένη λέγεται Δορκάς· αὕτη ἦν πλήρης ⸂ἔργων ἀγαθῶν⸃ καὶ ἐλεημοσυνῶν ὧν ἐποίει.

verses.restored: It happened in those days that she became weak and died. Washing her, they laid her in an upper room.

familiar.text: And it came to pass in those days, that she was sick, and died: whom when they had washed, they laid her in an upper chamber.

modern.text: At that time, however, she became sick and died, and her body was washed and placed in an upper room.

original.text: ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐκείναις ἀσθενήσασαν αὐτὴν ἀποθανεῖν· λούσαντες δὲ ⸂ἔθηκαν αὐτὴν⸃ ἐν ὑπερῴῳ.

verses.restored: Since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples, hearing that Peter was there, sent two men to him, urging, Do not delay coming to us.

familiar.text: And forasmuch as Lydda was nigh to Joppa, and the disciples had heard that Peter was there, they sent unto him two men, desiring him that he would not delay to come to them.

modern.text: Since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples heard that Peter was there and sent two men to urge him, “Come to us without delay.”

original.text: ἐγγὺς δὲ οὔσης Λύδδας τῇ Ἰόππῃ οἱ μαθηταὶ ἀκούσαντες ὅτι Πέτρος ἐστὶν ἐν αὐτῇ ἀπέστειλαν ⸂δύο ἄνδρας⸃ πρὸς αὐτὸν παρακαλοῦντες· Μὴ ⸀ὀκνήσῃς διελθεῖν ἕως ⸀ἡμῶν·

verses.restored: Peter rose and went with them. When he arrived, they brought him into the upper room, and all the widows stood beside him weeping and showing tunics and garments that Dorcas made while she was with them.

familiar.text: Then Peter arose and went with them. When he was come, they brought him into the upper chamber: and all the widows stood by him weeping, and shewing the coats and garments which Dorcas made, while she was with them.

modern.text: So Peter got up and went with them. On his arrival, they took him to the upper room. All the widows stood around him, weeping and showing him the tunics and other clothing that Dorcas had made while she was still with them.

original.text: ἀναστὰς δὲ Πέτρος συνῆλθεν αὐτοῖς· ὃν παραγενόμενον ἀνήγαγον εἰς τὸ ὑπερῷον, καὶ παρέστησαν αὐτῷ πᾶσαι αἱ χῆραι κλαίουσαι καὶ ἐπιδεικνύμεναι χιτῶνας καὶ ἱμάτια ὅσα ἐποίει μετʼ αὐτῶν οὖσα ἡ Δορκάς.

verses.restored: Peter put them all outside, knelt down, and prayed. Turning to the body, he said, Tabitha, rise. She opened her eyes, and seeing Peter, sat up.

familiar.text: But Peter put them all forth, and kneeled down, and prayed; and turning him to the body said, Tabitha, arise. And she opened her eyes: and when she saw Peter, she sat up.

modern.text: Then Peter sent them all out of the room. He knelt down and prayed, and turning toward her body, he said, “Tabitha, get up!” She opened her eyes, and seeing Peter, she sat up.

original.text: ἐκβαλὼν δὲ ἔξω πάντας ὁ Πέτρος ⸀καὶ θεὶς τὰ γόνατα προσηύξατο, καὶ ἐπιστρέψας πρὸς τὸ σῶμα εἶπεν· Ταβιθά, ἀνάστηθι. ἡ δὲ ἤνοιξεν τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῆς, καὶ ἰδοῦσα τὸν Πέτρον ἀνεκάθισεν.

verses.restored: Giving her his hand, he raised her; calling the holy ones and widows, he presented her alive.

familiar.text: And he gave her his hand, and lifted her up, and when he had called the saints and widows, presented her alive.

modern.text: Peter took her by the hand and helped her up. Then he called the saints and widows and presented her to them alive.

original.text: δοὺς δὲ αὐτῇ χεῖρα ἀνέστησεν αὐτήν, φωνήσας δὲ τοὺς ἁγίους καὶ τὰς χήρας παρέστησεν αὐτὴν ζῶσαν.

verses.restored: It became known throughout all Joppa, and many trusted in the Lord.

familiar.text: And it was known throughout all Joppa; and many believed in the Lord.

modern.text: This became known all over Joppa, and many people believed in the Lord.

original.text: γνωστὸν δὲ ἐγένετο καθʼ ὅλης ⸀τῆς Ἰόππης, καὶ ⸂ἐπίστευσαν πολλοὶ⸃ ἐπὶ τὸν κύριον.

verses.restored: It happened that he remained many days in Joppa with a certain Simon, a tanner.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, that he tarried many days in Joppa with one Simon a tanner.

modern.text: And Peter stayed for several days in Joppa with a tanner named Simon.

original.text: ἐγένετο ⸀δὲ ἡμέρας ἱκανὰς ⸀μεῖναι ἐν Ἰόππῃ παρά τινι Σίμωνι βυρσεῖ.
